output.summary: KEP-2261 proposes moving the mount library (k8s.io/utils/mount) into a k/k staging repo so it can be shared by in-tree plugins and external CSI drivers, using k/k e2e tests and infrastructure. Status is implementable, stage stable.
output.rationale: The mount library is used by in-tree volume plugins and external CSI drivers, but fixes cannot be backported to older releases without pulling in unrelated changes, and breaking changes in k8s/utils/mount were caught only after vendoring into Kubernetes. Moving it under k/k lets it use existing k/k tests and infrastructure while remaining easy to maintain. The source states the proposal and the 2021 discussion about whether the work is complete, but does not detail the remaining steps beyond that.

alternatives.option: Keep a separate repo under k8s for the library
alternatives.why_not: The design says this would still require heavy investment to build and maintain tests and infrastructure with the same coverage as k/k.

evidence.quote: We propose moving this library from k8s/utils to a separate k/k staging repo in order to leverage existing k/k e2e tests and infrastructure
We can't backport fixes to the mount library to older Kubernetes releases without potentially pulling in a number of unrelated and potentially breaking changes in other areas.
We can have a separate repo under k8s for the library, but the main drawbacks are that we would still need to invest heavily to build and maintain tests and infrastructure
I believe @brahmaroutu still has a few remaining PRs to wrap up the work
